etymologies.etymologyHTML: From French tarif, from Italian tariffa, from Ottoman Turkish تعرفه (ta'rife), from Persian تعرفه (ta'refe), from Arabic تَعْرِفَة (taʕrifa, “tariff, rate”), from the root ع ر ف (ʕ-r-f).

definitions.definition: A system of government-imposed duties levied on imported or exported goods; a list of such duties, or the duties themselves.

quote.citation: 2004, Michael B Gross, The war against Catholicism:
quote.text: For the sake of this support, the party advocated for agricultural tariffs, for antimargarine laws, and for restrictions on meat importation.

quote.citation: 2012, Bert van Selm, The Economics of Soviet Breakup:
quote.text: Possibly Wallonians bought goods in Flanders that they could have obtained cheaper in Holland if it were not for the tariff.

definitions.definition: A schedule of rates, fees or prices.

quote.citation: 1906, Department of Commerce and Labor. Bureau of Manufactures, Monthly Consular and Trade Reports (number 313, page 75)
quote.text: There is a tariff in every carriage, and most of them also have taxometers.

definitions.definition: (British) A sentence determined according to a scale of standard penalties for certain categories of crime.
